Proxies

proxy.Rd

Starts a local relay proxy for a named pipe. The relay proxy lives in a background process through r_bg.

Essentially, this is a way to communicate with named pipes through HTTP requests. The relay server takes HTTP requests from a client (e.g. with curl or httr2), sends them to the named pipe using a winpipe and then sends the response back to the HTTP client.

np_relay() is the workhorse function, which contains the server socket logic. np_proxy() is a simple wrapper that starts the relay server in a background process in order to not block the main session.

Usage

np_proxy(name, port = httpuv::randomPort(), relay = np_relay)

np_relay(name, port)

Arguments

name

[character(1)]

Pipe name, with or without the \\.\pipe\ prefix.

port

[numeric(1)]

TCP port that the relay server should listen on.

relay

[function]

A relay function that takes a named pipe name and a port and forwards requests and responses between a server and a client. Defaults to np_relay.

Value

np_proxy() returns an object of class winpipe_proxy. This object contains the base URL that accepts requests and a process object that manages the server child process. np_relay() returns nothing but runs a server that accepts requests as long as the function is running.

Examples

# np_proxy() is a good way to communicate with named pipes
# that communicate over HTTP, e.g., docker
if (np_exists("docker_engine") && requireNamespace("httr2")) {
library(httr2)

proxy <- np_proxy("docker_engine")

# GET requests, e.g., to query the docker version
resp <- request(proxy$base_url) %>%
  req_url_path("/version") %>%
  req_perform() %>%
  resp_body_json(resp)
resp[c("Version", "ApiVersion", "Os")]

# POST requests, e.g., to create a container
# do not run this if you don't wish to modify your docker state
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# pull image
pull <- request(proxy$base_url) %>%
  req_url_path("/images/create") %>%
  req_url_query(fromImage = "hello-world", tag = "latest") %>%
  req_method("POST") %>%
  req_perform()
pull$status_code

# create container
created <- request(proxy$base_url) %>%
  req_url_path("/containers/create") %>%
  req_url_query(name = "winpipe-test") %>%
  req_body_json(list(Image = "hello-world:latest")) %>%
  req_perform()
created$status_code
} # }
}
#> Error: object 'resp' not found
